title: 45 more mysteries
description: Stories 6 to 50, from The Haunted Mill to The Cursed Well: 45 more villages, each with two werewolves hiding among the villagers.

Yesterday evening at 8PM I was just kneading my dough! I was there all night, kneading away.
Lalala. I made a LOVELY batch of bread last night.
I knew it wasn't the fisherman, he is the least fishy guy I know! Last night I baked a fresh aromatic batch of dough.
I baked another bitingly good loaf of bread last night. Mmm
I always knew that fisherman was fishy!
I have a new idea for a recipe. Sourdough a la villager!
Last night I was extremely busy writing some new laws for our village!
I was at the Blue Moon Inn gloriously presenting our new law: mandatory late-night runs in the deep, dark woods.
I was at the blue moon inn gloriously presenting our new law. Mandatory late night runs in the deep dark woods!
I was going for a gallop in the deep dark woods last night.
Werewolf? I am just happy about our new jogging laws. Delicious!
What an awful time of the year for this to happen. This week is the fishing competition!
Despite the accident... Fishing spirits were high. Even the barmaid was watching... Intently!
I knew that beggar was a werewolf. Always licking his lips at the fish... And me!
The second the barmaid said she did not like fishing - I knew she was a werewolf!
I was looking at our fishing catches last night. I saw the barmaid licking her lips in the distance!
Last night I was trying to find the fish we caught! I bet the pesky beggar took them!
The barmaid keeps saying: Mmm delicious fisherman. It's really putting me off my game!
The fishing competition is ruined! Atleast... I am a winner by technicality.
The village is buzzing with the upcoming full moon festival. But with these strange happenings, I've been sticking close to the lake all night.
Festival preparations are in full swing, but everyone's behaving oddly. I saw shadows near the inn and the forge last night.
The blacksmith's constant hammering at odd hours sounded too much like beastly growls. I suspected him from the start!
I always thought the barmaid was suspicious, the way she poured drinks with that hungry look in her eyes. Knew she was a werewolf all along!
Last night while checking my nets, I spotted the barmaid wandering near the woods, her eyes reflecting the moonlight strangely.
I heard unusual clanging from the forge at midnight, as if the blacksmith was forging something sinister.
The barmaid has been muttering about 'thirsty for more than ale' during the festival. It's making me uneasy!
With so much chaos, at least the festival is wrapping up. Glad I've stayed out of trouble by the water.
Christmas is here! Secret Santa gifts are everywhere. I left a big fish for someone last night.
I saw the baker and beggar swap presents last night. Looked odd.
The beggar got my fish gift. He ate the wrapper too. I knew he was bad.
I knew the baker was a wolf. His present was a pie that smelled like meat, not fruit!
The baker gave everyone red cookies last night.
The beggar stole gifts from under the tree. I saw him run off.
The baker keeps saying his oven is hot for fresh meat. Not cookies!
Christmas is ruined. At least I still have my fish.
Last night I was inspecting the old mill. The council wants it torn down!
The farmer keeps blaming the mill spirits. Spirits don't leave paw prints!
I always said that mill was cursed, and the farmer knew it best!
I've ordered extra lanterns near the mill. Safety first!
A werewolf in MY village? This is a governance nightmare.
Somebody is haunting more than that mill, mark my words.
I declared the frozen lake off-limits after last night's... incident.
Someone left tracks across the ice. Big, clawed tracks.
Those footprints to the lake? The butcher's boots, no doubt!
A mayor must keep his village from thawing into chaos!
I've never trusted a quiet frozen lake.
I've, ahem, misplaced some village records. Nothing suspicious!
As mayor, I keep certain attack reports confidential. For morale!
The fisherman gone? We shared many... late night stories.
Amaya's paperwork is sacred. Stop snooping
Those records may have mentioned my... nightly habits.
The moon does strange things to a man. Allegedly.
The harvest festival must go on, werewolves or not!
The baker's new loaf tastes... gamey. What's in it?
No baker means the festival bread is cancelled. Tragic!
A golden harvest brings out the village's true colours.
I'll cut the ribbon myself. Carefully.
The village has gone eerily silent. Even the dogs won't bark.
The beggar claims to hear everything. Perhaps he hears too much.
The beggar gone? He knew too many secrets, that one.
Silence in a village means someone's keeping quiet.
I'll restore order, one hushed street at a time.
I ordered urgent repairs on the old castle. For, uh, historical reasons.
The castle needs restoring. Ignore the digging noises at night.
The blacksmith gone? We explored those tunnels together, sadly.
A mayor beautifies the village! Stop questioning the budget!
Perhaps I ordered those tunnels for... personal use.
The castle and I share many secrets. Ahem.
Complaints of howling near the river all night. Most disruptive!
The fisherman and beggar are always by that river. Suspicious pair.
The fisherman gone? The river's gone quiet too. Telling.
I'll station a guard by the water. If I can find a brave one.
A mayor's sleep matters too, you know!
The bakery bell rang at midnight again. Who rings a bell at MIDNIGHT?
The baker swears he doesn't ring it. Then who does?
No baker means no midnight bell. Peaceful, if grim.
A ringing bell is a signal. But to whom?
I'll have that bell confiscated by decree!
A shadow market has appeared after dark. Unlicensed. Unacceptable
The butcher sells meat I've never approved. What meat IS it?
No butcher, no shadow market. Case closed? Perhaps.
I'll regulate this midnight market into oblivion!
Commerce in shadows breeds trouble.
I'm hosting a moonlight race through the deep dark woods! For fun!
The race runs at midnight. Through the woods. Alone. Enjoy!
The farmer gone? He designed our lovely little race route.
A civic race builds community spirit! Nothing sinister!
Perhaps the race route leads runners... to me.
May the fastest villager survive— er, win!
Mining tools and fishing gear found together at the old cave. Curious.
The blacksmith's tools by a CAVE? He's no miner.
No blacksmith to explain those tools now. Convenient.
I'll seal that mine before anyone else wanders in.
Forgotten places hide unforgotten crimes.
Removing village records? Just... spring cleaning. In the archive. At night.
The records are being reorganized. Nothing about attacks, I assure you!
The baker gone? He lit such lovely candles for our... meetings.
A mayor manages archives! Stop rifling through my paperwork!
The records I burned mentioned some... nightly incidents.
What the village forgets can't hurt it. Heh.
A storm last night, yet the attacks continued. Rain won't stop a wolf.
The beggar shelters under bridges. Right where tracks were found.
The beggar gone? He knew every dry hiding spot in the rain.
I'll issue umbrellas AND a curfew. Order in all weather!
Rain washes away tracks. And alibis.
Reports of a 'secret garden' the farmer guards. On village land!
The farmer won't let me inspect his hidden garden. What grows there?
No farmer, no guarded garden. What was he hiding in there?
I'll survey that garden by decree. Nothing stays secret from me!
Secret gardens grow secret troubles.
I decreed a wolf-mask party! Everyone hides their face. Delightful!
A masked party means no one sees who slips out. How fun!
The blacksmith gone? He wore such a convincing wolf mask. Too convincing.
A mayor throws grand parties! Stop reading into it!
My mask wasn't... entirely a mask. Ahem.
Best costume goes to the most... convincing wolf.
The village lanterns keep vanishing near the river and bakery. Sabotage!
The fisherman and baker's areas lose the most lanterns. Coincidence?
With the fisherman gone, no more lanterns have vanished. Hmm.
No lanterns means darkness. And darkness means wolves.
Someone WANTS this village blind.
I run the midnight market. For commerce! Whatever a villager needs at midnight, I supply.
I control who trades after dark. And what... disappears. Ahem.
The beggar gone? He traded such useful... secrets at my market.
A mayor regulates trade! There's nothing sinister here!
Some of my market 'goods' had a pulse. Recently.
The midnight market never closes. For SOME customers.
The storm destroyed most evidence. But muddy footprints remain!
The footprints match the butcher's boots. And the farmer's.
No butcher, and yet those big boot prints stopped appearing. Hmm.
Mud tells the truth even when people don't.
A storm can't wash away guilt entirely.
Strange wolf-shaped tools were found in the forge. Most alarming!
The blacksmith forges wolf-shaped implements. Why, exactly?
With the blacksmith gone, who made those wolf tools? A mystery.
I'll have that forge inspected top to bottom.
A craftsman reveals himself in his craft.
The village anniversary will be UNFORGETTABLE. I've planned everything.
The whole village gathered in one place at night. How convenient. Ahem.
The barmaid gone? She helped me plan such a... memorable feast.
A mayor honours tradition! This is a CELEBRATION, not a scheme!
Perhaps the celebration was a trap. My trap.
To the village! May MOST of you see next year.
A broken boat washed ashore, full of clues pointing to the forge.
The fisherman's boat broke apart, and inside were the blacksmith's tools!
With the fisherman gone, the boat mystery goes quiet.
Boats and forges shouldn't share secrets.
A wreck always tells a tale.
Red bread from the baker, mystery meat from the butcher. I'm concerned.
The baker's bread is suspiciously RED. What's the ingredient?
No baker, no red bread. The village menu improves already.
Food this strange demands an investigation.
You are what you bake. And sell.
The old barn stands empty, yet lights flicker in it at night.
The farmer owns that barn but swears it's abandoned. Is it?
With the farmer gone, the barn's finally dark. Interesting.
I'll have that barn searched from rafter to floor.
Empty barns make excellent hiding places.
I've asked villagers to gather firewood in the whispering woods. At night. For thrift!
The woods are perfectly safe! Ignore the whispers. And the fisherman.
The fisherman gone? He watched the woods so... attentively for me.
A mayor promotes self-sufficiency! Gather that wood!
I send them into the woods because I'm... waiting there.
The woods whisper my name. How flattering. Ahem.
Under the silver moon, howls echo between the inn and the forge.
The howls bounce from the barmaid's inn to the blacksmith's forge.
With the barmaid gone, the inn's gone quiet under the moon.
A silver moon reveals silver truths.
Two buildings, one howl. Curious.
A grand feast, yet clues to the attacks were hidden right in the food!
The baker's feast dishes hid the strangest ingredients.
No baker means no feast. And no more poisoned platters, perhaps.
I'll have every dish inspected before the next feast.
A feast can feed a village or a beast.
The village tournament begins! Feats of strength, all in good fun.
The farmer and butcher dominate every event. Suspiciously strong.
With the farmer gone, the tournament's oddly safer. Hmm.
A tournament reveals a village's true champions. And villains.
Competition brings out the beast in some.
I've been visiting the old lighthouse. For, ah, maritime administration. At night.
The lighthouse is official business! The fisherman merely assists.
The fisherman gone? We held such productive meetings at the lighthouse.
A mayor oversees the coast! The lighthouse is MINE to visit!
The lighthouse is where I meet my... associate. To plan.
The lighthouse beam hides more than it shows.
The baker's secret recipe was stolen. And oh, what strange ingredients!
The baker guards a recipe with ingredients I dare not name.
No baker, no secret recipe. Perhaps that's for the best.
I'll have that recipe examined by the council.
Some recipes should stay secret. Buried, even.
The blacksmith forges weapons, the butcher stockpiles meat. For what war?
The blacksmith's secret armory and the butcher's meat pile alarm me.
With the blacksmith gone, the weapon-hoarding stopped. Telling.
I'll requisition both their stores at once.
Weapons and meat make a grim pairing.
The river festival draws the whole village to the water at dusk.
The fisherman runs the festival, the barmaid the refreshments. Cozy.
With the fisherman gone, the festival lost its... predator. Hmm.
I'll station guards along the riverbank this year.
A festival by dark water invites dark deeds.
The harvest moon festival is upon us. May it be safe. It won't be.
The farmer and baker host the harvest moon feast. Under a FULL moon.
With the farmer gone, the harvest moon feels less... hungry.
I'll shorten the festivities. Home before moonrise!
A harvest moon feeds more than the fields.
The old tower is locked for public safety. Nothing to see. Move along!
The tower stays LOCKED by my order. Its contents are... classified.
The blacksmith gone? He made the only key to my tower. Pity.
A mayor secures dangerous structures! Stop prying!
The tower holds evidence. Against me. That's why it's locked.
What's in the tower stays in the tower.
Snow blankets the village, yet strange tracks cut right through it.
The tracks in the snow lead from the beggar's spot to the river.
With the beggar gone, no fresh tracks in the snow. Curious.
Fresh snow keeps an honest record.
Winter hides nothing for long.
The midnight train is a triumph of my administration! It runs so... discreetly.
The train lets a man leave and return unseen. For BUSINESS, of course.
The butcher gone? He rode the midnight train with me so often.
A mayor builds infrastructure! The train is PROGRESS!
The train's my escape route. After... certain nights.
All aboard the midnight train. Mind the... remains.
A treasure hunt for the village founding! Everyone's out digging. At night.
The blacksmith forged the treasure clues. The beggar hid them. Cozy.
With the blacksmith gone, the treasure maps stopped appearing. Odd.
I'll oversee this treasure hunt personally.
Some hunts dig up more than gold.
The inn is said to be haunted now. Guests check in and never check out!
The barmaid runs that inn, the fisherman drinks there nightly. Cozy pair.
With the barmaid gone, the inn's 'hauntings' have ceased. Telling.
I'll have the inn investigated. Ghosts don't leave claw marks.
A haunted inn is often just a hungry one.
The crystal cave glitters with clues, and half of them lead to the forge.
The farmer guards the cave, the blacksmith's tools litter it. Why?
With the farmer gone, no one guards the crystal cave. Interesting.
I'll have that cave surveyed by torchlight.
Even crystal can't hide a dark deed.
The red moon rises tonight. A rare omen! I've, ah, cleared my schedule.
The red moon is just a natural wonder! Everyone stay in. Except me.
The baker gone? We so enjoyed the red moon together, he and I.
A mayor observes celestial events! It's SCIENCE!
The red moon does something to me. And to my... appetite.
Bask in the red moon, villagers. While you can.
A travelling circus arrived. The whole village is dazzled. Perhaps too dazzled.
The butcher supplies the circus meat, the barmaid the drinks. Cozy.
With the butcher gone, the circus lost its... backstage helper. Hmm.
I'll keep a close eye on this circus.
A circus is all misdirection. Perfect for a wolf.
A secret tunnel was found, running from the river straight to the forge.
The tunnel links the fisherman's river to the blacksmith's forge. Why?
With the fisherman gone, the tunnel's gone silent. Telling.
I'll have that tunnel sealed and searched.
Secret tunnels lead to secret crimes.
Tonight I crown the village's honorary king! A golden crown, a grand ceremony.
The whole village gathers for the crowning. At night. How... convenient.
The beggar gone? He helped me plan the ceremony from the shadows.
A mayor honours tradition with pomp! Nothing more!
The ceremony's a cover. For me. You've nearly got it.
Long live the king! And the... crowd. For now.
The final festival of the season is tonight. May we all survive it.
The farmer runs the festival games, the barmaid the bar. Cozy pair.
With the farmer gone, the final festival feels safer already.
